chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has dirhams owed to him by another man, and he gifts them to him; is it for him to return to them? He said: No. The ruling in this narration is also as we said in the previous narrations, equally. And it is also possible that it is to be understood as referring to preference (istihbab).
ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke a gift of money if it was a debt owed to them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a creditor gifts a debt owed to him, the transfer is final and he cannot retract it, establishing the principle of irrevocability in such gifts. The text further contextualizes this by linking it to earlier narrations and suggesting the ruling may be rooted in *istihbab* (recommendation), reflecting the nuanced juristic approach to debt forgiveness as a charitable act. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the finality of gift contracts (*hibah*) even when the subject matter is a financial obligation.
